name: Turkmenistan
region: Nationwide — Ashgabat, Balkan, Lebap, Dashoguz regions
summary: Turkmenistan holds a Freedom House score of 2/100 — tied for the lowest globally. 72,000 people are estimated to live in modern slavery. 162 cases of forcibly disappeared prisoners are documented. Systemic forced cotton labor, banned US imports, and ranked 175th/180 for press freedom make this one of the world's most closed and repressive societies.
context:
Turkmenistan is one of the world's most closed and repressive states — a Central Asian petrostate ruled by a dynastic dictatorship since independence from the Soviet Union in 1991. It ranks alongside North Korea and Eritrea at the very bottom of global freedom indices.

The country's Freedom House score of 2/100 reflects an almost total absence of political and civil freedoms. There are no independent political parties, no free media, no civil society organizations, and no independent judiciary. State media projects an image of prosperity and order while citizens live under pervasive surveillance and fear.

The forced cotton labor system is one of Turkmenistan's most documented human rights abuses. The government mobilizes hundreds of thousands of citizens — including students, teachers, and doctors — to pick cotton under threat of job loss or worse. This system is so egregious that the United States banned all Turkmenistan cotton imports in 2018. The use of forced labor in the cotton supply chain makes Turkmenistan-sourced cotton untouchable for ethical supply chains.

An estimated 72,000 people live in modern slavery conditions, according to the Global Slavery Index. Prisoners — including political prisoners — are frequently held incommunicado in conditions described as torture. 162 cases of 'disappeared' prisoners have been formally documented, where families receive no information about whether their relative is alive or dead.

Turkmenistan's gas reserves — among the world's largest — have provided the government with resources to maintain control and resist international pressure. Gas revenues fund an elaborate personality cult and massive public construction projects while basic goods are rationed or unavailable.

donate.name: Amnesty International — Turkmenistan
donate.description: Campaigning for the release of political prisoners and an end to enforced disappearances in Turkmenistan's prison system.

donate.name: Prove They Are Alive! Campaign
donate.description: An international campaign for disappeared prisoners in Turkmenistan, demanding the government confirm whether prisoners are alive and their conditions.

awareness: Share that Turkmenistan's Freedom House score is 2/100 — essentially zero — and ask why this receives no international attention
Highlight the forced cotton harvest: every year, hundreds of thousands of Turkmen are compelled to pick cotton under threat of punishment — this is modern slavery at industrial scale
Amplify reporting from Turkmen exile journalists and the Turkmen Helsinki Foundation, which documents abuses from outside the country
Raise awareness about the 'disappeared' prisoners: 162 documented cases of families with no information about whether their relatives are alive after years of imprisonment
Challenge companies that may source from Turkmenistan's gas sector to examine whether their supply chains fund a system of modern slavery
political: Urge your government to raise Turkmenistan's human rights record in all energy and trade discussions — the country's gas wealth cannot be an excuse for silence
Push for bilateral sanctions targeting Turkmenistan's ruling family and officials responsible for forced labor and enforced disappearances
Advocate for support for Turkmen exile journalists and civil society organizations that are the only source of independent information
Demand that the EU condition energy partnership agreements with Turkmenistan on measurable improvements in forced labor and prison conditions
Support UN mechanisms addressing the 'disappeared' prisoners and push Turkmenistan to account for each documented case
